records.rule: Account owns customer/account/beneficiary lifecycle; Payments owns transaction/reservation authority; Ledger owns monetary truth.
Only Ledger owns postings, balances, holds and durable monetary receipts.
Header, every posting leg, authority evidence and durable receipt commit atomically or none become visible.
After SQL commit, redelivery recovers the committed result rather than executing the banking event again.
A hold reduces available funds but is not a Ledger posting; reservation state/event/evidence/receipt commit atomically.
Customer intent, physical cash fact and Ledger monetary truth are distinct facts that must be correlated.
Staff payments use a separate authenticated ingress with exact Staff Authority evidence; Staff Channel is not monetary authority.
Teller Till owns physical counter-cash custody and never customer account or Ledger truth.
Branch Cash owns physical custody; released cash remains explicit in-transit custody until accepted.
Branch Day certifies opening/closing from typed evidence and is blocked by in-transit cash, unresolved reconciliation or discrepancy.
Offline ATM vending requires retained bank-issued, bounded, single-use authority; terminal assertions are evidence, not authority.
Already-incurred physical obligations may require explicit SETTLEMENT_MUST_POST authority; there is no generic force=true capability.
Merchant Banking owns derivative/margin/close-out facts but is at arm’s length from Core/Retail and cannot post the Core Ledger.
Merchant collateral candidate is not usable collateral until Core returns exact enforceable control evidence.
Merchant close-out may create a contractual settlement obligation; Core collateral realisation/cash movement is a separate Core authority event.
FX journals balance independently per currency; unlike currencies are never summed together, and both Legal Effects are evaluated.
Fees are a separate Institutional Policy decision and are committed atomically with the transfer when applicable.
Limits/fees/reservations/account-opening rules belong to Institutional Policy; legal/regulatory effects are evaluated separately; fixture values are not real regulation.
No transfer credit may become ordinary spendable balance unless the balancing debit is authoritative in the same Ledger transaction.
Internal settlement, fee and FX accounts are Ledger-owned infrastructure; channels do not nominate arbitrary internal GL identifiers.
Inspect the newest supplied package before coding; revise the smallest sphere object and attach structured provenance.
